chapter_title: Concerning the Purification of these Four Elements [that have been place]d in the Flesh
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by the oldest teaching layer. The core is a systematic four-element body-cosmos correspondence: each of four elements (fire, water, light, wind/tree) disgorges a three-fold pollution chain (bodily emission → emotion → physical condition), yielding twelve emissions total. This is classic correspondential substrate — both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. The NLP pipeline's substrate vocabulary (zoomorphic, metal terms) does not fire because this chapter uses a DIFFERENT substrate register: element→body→emotion correspondences. The only non-substrate material is the dialogue frame (¶1) and the institutional application in ¶9 (elect/sinners). The chapter is compact, structurally complete, and remarkably uncontaminated by editorial extension.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic frame: 'the apostle is sitting among the congregation. He speaks thus.' No cosmological content whatsoever. High institutional score (17.65) from 'apostle' and 'congregation.'

paragraphs.core_text: The four elements [are what is] purified. From the beginning they are holy ones, living ones, and enlighteners. However, when they undertood [ ... ] in that first struggle, the waste was [mixed] in with them, and the darkness of the enemy was mixed with them. And when they were come into the body, stripping off these polluted garments, they set them in the flesh. Their pollutions, which they have stripped off, shall be displayed in a [ ... ] and become a danger to the body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Establishes the cosmological framework: four elements descended, became mixed with Darkness in the first struggle, entered the body, stripped off pollutions. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. 'That first struggle' references the primordial cosmological conflict — substrate language. The voice is impersonal and process-oriented.

paragraphs.core_text: The discharge of this pollution, that [the fir]e shall disgorge and place in the body, is [blo]od. The discharge of the blood is anger. The discharge of anger is the humours.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First element-body correspondence chain: fire → blood → anger → humours. Three-fold systematic mapping. Both sides internal to the cosmic-bodily system. Classic correspondential structure: element mapped to bodily emission, then to emotion, then to physical condition.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.240⟩
Also, the emissions that the waters discharge from them are lust. The discharge of lust is bitterness. The emission of bitterness is f[e]ver.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second chain: water → lust → bitterness → fever. Same three-fold structure. 'Also' is a continuation marker within the enumeration, not an editorial bridge. Note the variation between 'discharge' and 'emission' — may reflect Coptic translation choices for different terms in the source.

paragraphs.core_text: The emission that light shall disgorge is flesh. The emission of flesh is gloom. [The] emission of gloom is obstinacy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third chain: light → flesh → gloom → obstinacy. Same three-fold structure maintained. The correspondence of light-element to flesh is notable — the physical body as the 'garment' of light is a deep correspondential concept.

paragraphs.core_text: The emissions that the tree shall disgorge, they are the voices of the winds of shame. The emission of winds of shame [is ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth chain: wind/tree → winds of shame → [fragmentary]. Gardner notes 'the tree' is unclear but the fourth element must be wind. The text becomes fragmentary here. 'Tree' as a designation for wind is unusual — possibly a translation artifact or textual corruption. The three-fold structure is interrupted by lacuna.

paragraphs.core_text: The emission of the [tear] is the [ ... ] of these twelve emissions.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary statement: 'twelve emissions' (4 elements × 3 emissions each). This confirms the systematic structure of the teaching. Despite heavy lacunae, the summary number '12' proves the four three-fold chains were the intended structure. '[tear]' may be the missing third term of the fourth chain.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] these four elements shall [ ... ] what are gathered in are [f]ound by the management of this soul food [that] enters the body. When they enter the body, they are cleansed and purified and established [i]n their living image, which is the new man. They shall live [ ... ] and receive the Light Mind and be purified in their image; and they come forth, being cleansed and holy. They attain their first rest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Describes the cosmological purification process: elements gathered via food, enter body, cleansed, established in 'living image,' receive Light Mind, come forth holy, attain rest. Both sides of all mappings stay within the cosmic system. 'Soul food' functions as a cosmological mechanism term (light-in-matter), not an institutional prescription. 'New man' names the reconstituted light form. 'Light Mind' (Nous) is a cosmological entity. Some terms (new man, Light Mind) may be Manichaean-specific vocabulary layered onto an older process teaching, but the PROCESS described (element-gathering → purification → reconstitution → ascent) is substrate. Substrate score 2.56 confirms presence of oldest-layer vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: they shall be cleansed and go u[p to] the land of the living ones; but these that come to [ ... ] and pass through them and [ ... / ... ] in sins. Their end will occur in transmigration and spirit.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'So, when they shall reach the elect, this is how' — bridge connective 'So' + institutional category 'the elect' applies the cosmic process to a Manichaean institutional class. Removed 'the sinners' — institutional moral category. These reach outside the cosmic system into the contemporary Manichaean community structure.
paragraphs.temporal_note: This paragraph bridges the substrate teaching to its institutional application. 'The elect' and 'sinners' are Manichaean institutional categories. But 'the land of the living ones' and 'transmigration' are cosmological substrate — the two fates of the elements (ascent vs. continued cycling). Institutional score 3.7 confirms the institutional vocabulary presence. The substrate teaching embedded here: purified elements ascend; unpurified elements continue in transmigration.
